candidate_relations.reason: Ichthyosis vulgaris is a diffuse scaling disorder and does not produce homogenized papillary dermal collagen with follicular plugs.
Darier disease shows acantholytic dyskeratosis, not follicular plugging with atrophic epidermis and homogenized collagen.
Unspecified ichthyosis likewise fails to explain steroid-responsive hypopigmented folliculocentric papules with LS histology.
A sparse bandlike lymphocytic infiltrate is a lichenoid dermatitis component but omits the follicular LSA collagen homogenization.
Pityriasis rubra pilaris produces follicular orange-red papules and palmoplantar keratoderma, not atrophic LS histology.
Keratosis pilaris can look folliculocentric clinically but lacks epidermal atrophy and homogenized papillary collagen.
Scleroderma/morphea scleroses deeper dermis, whereas this biopsy shows papillary homogenization, follicular plugs, and lichenoid inflammation of LSA.
Lichen planopilaris is a scarring follicular lichenoid disease of hair-bearing scalp, not truncal hypopigmented keratotic LS papules.
Phrynoderma is a nutritional follicular keratotic eruption without LS collagen change or steroid-responsive atrophy.
Lichen spinulosus produces spiny follicular plugs without homogenized collagen, edema, and bandlike lymphocytes of LSA.
Lichen planus is a different lichenoid disease and would not show marked papillary dermal homogenization with follicular orthokeratotic plugs.
Dermatophytosis is not supported; there is no KOH/culture, and Congo-red-negative homogenized collagen is an LSA pattern.
Psoriasis would produce silvery plaques with neutrophils in the stratum corneum, not steroid-responsive hypopigmented folliculocentric papules whose dermoscopy shows central keratin plugs.

case_quality_flags: Histology shows folliculocentric lichen sclerosus, but no candidate names lichen sclerosus et atrophicus.
